sections.title: Entry requirements for Spain
sections.body: EU and Schengen citizens need only an ID card; everyone else needs a passport valid for three months beyond departure. Be prepared for possible additional checks depending on your nationality.
sections.source: the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs

sections.title: May weather in Barcelona
sections.body: May brings warm temperatures averaging 20-25°C (68-77°F) with little rain, making it ideal for enjoying outdoor activities. Days are long, with daylight lasting until around 9 PM, so pack light clothing and a light jacket for cooler evenings.

sections.title: How to pay and daily costs
sections.body: Cash is accepted but cards are widely used in most places, especially in tourist areas. Expect to spend around €60-€100 a day for two people, including meals and transport. Small local eateries may only accept cash, so having some on hand is advisable.

sections.title: Getting from the airport to the city
sections.body: The most convenient way from El Prat Airport to the city is via the Aerobus, costing around €5.90 per person and taking about 35 minutes to reach Plaça de Catalunya. Taxis are available but more expensive, around €30-€35.

sections.title: Navigating Barcelona easily
sections.body: Barcelona is quite walkable, especially in neighborhoods like the Gothic Quarter and Eixample. Consider a T10 card for the metro and bus system which allows for 10 rides for about €11.35, ideal for couples.
bullets: Metro operates from 5 AM to midnight

sections.title: Dining culture and meal times
sections.body: Lunch is typically served from 1 PM to 4 PM, and dinner from 8 PM onwards. Local street food, like tapas, is popular and can be found throughout the city. Don’t miss trying patatas bravas or jamón ibérico at local tapas bars.

sections.title: Some local etiquette tips
sections.body: It's customary to greet with a friendly 'Hola' and thank people with 'Gracias'. Don't be surprised if shops close in the afternoon for a siesta, usually between 2 PM and 5 PM.

sections.title: Health considerations and vaccinations
sections.body: It's advisable to have regular vaccinations up to date. Check for any required vaccinations, though none are mandatory for travel to Spain. Travel insurance is highly recommended for peace of mind.
sections.source: the CDC or your country's health department

sections.title: Emergency numbers and personal safety
sections.body: In case of emergencies, dial 112 for police, fire, or ambulance services. Barcelona is generally safe, but be mindful of your belongings in crowded areas to avoid pickpockets.

sections.title: Intercity travel options
sections.body: For day trips outside Barcelona, Renfe trains are your best bet, with regular services to places like Montserrat and Sitges. Tickets can be purchased online or at the station.

sections.title: Mobile data and SIM cards
sections.body: Purchasing a local SIM card is easy, with options available at the airport or stores in the city. Companies like Vodafone and Orange offer affordable data plans for travelers, and Wi-Fi is common in cafes and public spaces.
